cases.desc: Modifications to Previously approved Preliminary and Final Major Site Plan and Site Plan Amendment

The Owners seek to renovate and expand the existing residential structure at Block 11402, Lot 21 within the Harsimus Cove Historic District. This proposal involves a strategic vertical and horizontal expansion that increases the Gross Building Area to 6,265 SF while strictly maintaining the currently permitted density of four dwelling units. The design is deeply rooted in the context of its immediate neighbors, seeking to harmonize with the historic street wall and overall fabric of the block. Notably, the project achieves a significant public benefit by reducing existing non-conforming lot coverage from 100% to 93%, thereby increasing permeable open space and improving local site drainage. The requested variances are necessitated by the unique practical constraints of the Harsimus Cove Historic District and are consistent with established neighborhood patterns: Front & Rear Setbacks (c variance): The 12 ft front setback is maintained to preserve the existing property line relationship, but its interaction with the horizontal expansion requires a rear yard of 22 ft. This is a "flexible c" variance justified by the neighborhood context: multiple properties on this specific block already maintain rear setbacks significantly below the 30 ft requirement. Aligning with these existing conditions allows for a building footprint that is consistent with the historic "street wall" and density of the adjacent structures. Building Height (c/d variance): The proposed height of 45.83 ft represents a modest 5.83 ft (approx. 14%) deviation from the 40 ft limit. This vertical expansion is critical to facilitating high-quality, family-sized housing (including 3 and 4-bedroom layouts) within the existing unit count. This avoids the "over-densification" of the neighborhood while providing modern, viable residential spaces. Negative Criteria & Public Good: The proposal satisfies the "negative criteria" as it imposes no substantial detriment to the public good. Rather, it advances the purposes of the Municipal Land Use Law (MLUL) by promoting a desirable visual environment, preserving a historic structure through adaptive reuse, and improving environmental site conditions via reduced lot coverage. Representation Disclosure: The owners, Girish Shahdadpuri and Harish Pehlajani, are the individual owners of the subject property and are applying in their personal capacity rather than through a business entity (LLC or Corporation). In accordance with New Jersey Court Rule 1:21-1 and guidance provided by the Planning Department, we are exercising our right to represent ourselves pro se. While we have provided our own contact information in the attorney/representative fields to fulfill form requirements, we remain open to retaining counsel should the Board determine it necessary for this specific application.
